answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Sextant maker inked survey record filed with the boundary record flips the bet — each inked survey is a coastal chart countersigned by the warden, so a farm must calibrate a hundred real sextants by hand — and the willow lands on the attacker instead. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the vertex of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one. The ivory is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
